biggest_catch: OneHourTranslation no longer exists as a public translator-facing brand — its public web presence has folded into BLEND (getblend.com), which publishes no translator pay rates, so there is no official pay figure anywhere to verify.
catches: No official published translator pay figure exists — the OHT-era '100 credits = $1' system is documented only by third-party review sites, not official pages.
The brand has been absorbed into BLEND (getblend.com); translator recruitment now runs through an agency vendor network with no public per-word rates.
Historically translators were exam-certified native speakers (per third-party sources) — high qualification bar, never confirmed on official pages.
Zero guaranteed tasks; work depended on job availability and client approval quality ratings.
Could not confirm official payout method, minimums, or timing.
Third-party sources cite historical rates around $0.05/word and a $20 PayPal minimum, but none of this is official.

c1.evidence: One Hour Translation was a real company (founded 2008), now part of BLEND; no live official translator-pay page could be found.

c2.evidence: No official page describing translator pay could be located — only BLEND client-facing marketing pages and third-party reviews.

c3.evidence: No evidence of any upfront fee, but with no official translator program page, this cannot be confirmed from the provider.

c4.evidence: No official published pay figure found anywhere — per-word rates and payout thresholds exist only in third-party write-ups.

eligibility: Could not be confirmed from official pages. Third-party sources describe OHT-era translators as certified native speakers who passed an exam.
notes: Searched the web for an official onehourtranslation.com / blend.com translator-pay page: none found. getblend.com pages are client-facing marketing (documents, legal translation, TMS integrations) with no translator recruitment or pay info. Historical OHT translator mechanics (credits system, $20 PayPal minimum, exam requirement) appear only on third-party sites (webemployed.com, moneymakerland.com). Could not confirm the catalog's $0 claim from official pages at all — there is no official page stating any payout.
